A vectorized construction: for embeddings X[B,L,D], validity m and K≥1, compute counts c=cumsum(m) and zero-prefixed sums P=cat([0,cumsum(X*m[...,None])]). Set r=(c-K).clamp_min(0), j=where(r>0,searchsorted(c,r,right=False)+1,0), then Y=(P[:,1:]-gather(P,j[...,None].expand(-1,-1,D)))/c.clamp(1,K)[...,None]. This includes the current valid embedding, skips internal gaps, handles left padding, and returns zero for empty histories. Explicitly mask padded outputs if the queue reference does so. This construction follows documented [cumsum](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.9/generated/torch.cumsum.html), [searchsorted](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.9/generated/torch.searchsorted.html), and [gather](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.9/generated/torch.gather.html) semantics; floating-point work/storage is O(BLD), avoiding a B×L×K×D intermediate. Actual speed requires measurement.

Compare against a differentiable per-row queue using float64: random masks, internal gaps, all-padding rows, K=1, K>L, repeated items, and short histories. Check outputs and input gradients under identical random upstream gradients; verify zero gradients to padding and future positions. Run [gradcheck](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.9/generated/torch.autograd.gradcheck.gradcheck.html) with fixed masks. Repeat in production dtypes, reporting absolute/relative errors; FP32 prefix accumulation helps reduced-precision inputs, though prefix subtraction can suffer cancellation.

Benchmark representative B,L,D,K and padding densities after warmup. Measure forward, backward, and combined execution separately using CUDA events with synchronization, or [torch.utils.benchmark](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/recipes/recipes/benchmark.html); exclude compilation and data transfer. Rebuild graphs and clear gradients consistently. Synchronize, record baseline allocated bytes, reset peak-memory statistics, run forward/backward, synchronize, and report max_memory_allocated minus baseline plus absolute peak. Distinguish allocated from reserved memory ([CUDA documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda)). Report repeated timing medians and variability; no implementation is established as faster without these measurements.
